title: Microsoft Entra: stricter default blocks cross-domain federated sign-ins
summary: The roadmap facts, stricter default, policy update operations and portal monitoring path are supported. The categorical statement about no new data access lacks an explicit source; the beta permission documentation and the licensing prerequisite for Graph log access also need clarification.

claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Entra"]

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-07-01T23:03:18.
Microsoft plans to change the default policy rule to block cross-domain federated logins.
claims.quote: we will change the default rule for federatedTokenValidationPolicy to block logins where internalDomainFederation does not match UPN domain.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes manual tenant configuration as the current way to prohibit cross-domain logins.
claims.quote: The feature by default requires manual configuration in the tenant to prohibit cross-domain logins.

claims.claim: The internalDomainFederation object is typically created automatically during federation setup with AD FS or other identity providers.
claims.quote: This internalDomainFederation object is typically created automatically during federation setup with AD federation server or other IdPs.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The change starts enforcing stricter domain matching by default, so its arrival default is on.
claims.quote: Microsoft uses a stricter default that blocks cross-domain sign-ins when the federation realm root domain and the mapped user UPN root domain don't match.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enforced validation rejects a federated sign-in when its trusted realm root domain differs from the mapped user's UPN root domain.
claims.quote: If the root domains match, sign-in can continue, subject to all other authentication and policy checks. If the root domains don't match, Microsoft Entra ID rejects the authentication request.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[1].governs; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A request blocked by this policy is expected to return AADSTS5000820.
claims.quote: A blocked authentication request is expected to return error `AADSTS5000820`: **Sign-in blocked by Federated Token Validation policy. Contact your administrator for details.**

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The error message tells the blocked user to contact their administrator for details.
claims.quote: Sign-in blocked by Federated Token Validation policy. Contact your administrator for details.

claims.claim: The default change applies to federated domains with an associated internalDomainFederation object.
claims.quote: The change applies to federated domains that have an associated `internalDomainFederation` object.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The comparison treats child.contoso.com as the contoso.com root domain.
claims.quote: A child domain such as `child.contoso.com` resolves to the `contoso.com` root domain for this comparison.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The feature guide and beta reference describe the policy APIs on /beta as preview.
claims.quote: The `federatedTokenValidationPolicy` resource and its related Microsoft Graph APIs are available in preview through the `/beta` endpoint.

claims.claim: The guide says use of the preview APIs in production applications is unsupported.
claims.quote: Preview APIs are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications isn't supported.

claims.claim: A custom validatingDomains configuration can permit intentional cross-domain sign-in.
claims.quote: Yes. An administrator can allow cross-domain sign-in by configuring the `validatingDomains` resource to use a less-restrictive setting, including [`none`](strengthen-federated-sign-in-security#none).

claims.claim: Allowing cross-domain sign-in restores previous behaviour and removes this additional domain-consistency validation.
claims.quote: However, allowing cross-domain sign-in restores previous behavior and removes this additional domain-consistency validation layer.

claims.claim: validatingDomains.rootDomains accepts all, allFederated, allManaged, enumerated, allManagedAndEnumeratedFederated and none.
claims.quote: The `rootDomains` property defines the types of domains to which validation applies.

claims.claim: The policy's domain-validation configuration has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Validates every verified domain in the tenant. This option provides the broadest domain-consistency validation.

claims.claim: PUT /beta/policies/federatedTokenValidationPolicy updates the validatingDomains property controlling domain validation.
claims.quote: PUT https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/policies/federatedTokenValidationPolicy
claims.fix: Prefer the already-cited v1.0 operation: set controls[0].api.call to 'PUT /v1.0/policies/federatedTokenValidationPolicy' and its docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/federatedtokenvalidationpolicy-update?view=graph-rest-1.0; remove 'Preview (beta).' from this row's note. The beta reference lists all permission types as 'Not supported.' despite its delegated-role guidance, whereas the v1.0 reference documents Policy.ReadWrite.FedTokenValidation for delegated and application access.

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI setting for this policy is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "federatedTokenValidationPolicy" "admin center" configure portal. Opened the feature guide and beta/v1.0 update references; they document Graph operations, not a portal setting.

claims.claim: The portal path to sign-in logs is Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs.
claims.quote: Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**.

claims.claim: GET /v1.0/auditLogs/signIns retrieves tenant user sign-in logs for monitoring rather than changing the policy.
claims.quote: Retrieve the Microsoft Entra user [sign-ins](resources/signin?view=graph-rest-1.0) for your tenant.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-analyze-activity-logs-with-microsoft-graph to sources and append to controls[1].note: 'Graph access to sign-in reports requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licence.' This is an existing reporting prerequisite, not a published licence requirement for the new policy default itself.

claims.claim: Portal access to sign-in logs requires at least Reports Reader.
claims.quote: Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Reports Reader](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#reports-reader).

claims.claim: An attacker controlling a trusted federation realm could assert a known target source anchor to map a token to an account in another root domain.
claims.quote: If all prerequisites are met, an attacker who controls one trusted federation realm might attempt to issue a token that maps to a user in another realm by asserting that user's [source anchor](../hybrid/connect/plan-connect-design-concepts#sourceanchor).

claims.claim: Strict domain matching helps block cross-realm impersonation and is particularly useful in tenants with multiple federated domains.
claims.quote: This protection is especially useful in tenants with multiple federated domains because it helps reduce the blast radius of a compromised or misconfigured federated identity provider.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn lists mergers and acquisitions, coexistence, shared identity providers and migration projects as cross-domain dependency scenarios to review.
claims.quote:
Review intentional cross-domain sign-in scenarios, including:
- Mergers and acquisitions.
- Coexistence environments.
- Shared identity providers.
- Migration projects.

claims.claim: The extra validation occurs when Entra validates and maps a token returned after the identity provider authenticates the user.
claims.quote: The identity provider continues to perform its configured authentication. The additional protection is applied when Microsoft Entra ID validates and maps the returned federation token.

claims.claim: The policy does not change how the identity provider authenticates the user.
claims.quote:
### Does this change how the identity provider authenticates the user?

No. The identity provider continues to perform its configured authentication.

claims.claim: The change introduces no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: "federatedTokenValidationPolicy" "data access" autonomous account actions. Read the feature guide and policy resource/update references; they describe token validation but do not explicitly establish no new data access.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new data access:' and retain the supported sentence: 'The policy changes how Microsoft Entra ID validates a federation token after the identity provider has authenticated the user.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: After enforcement, administrators can monitor sign-in logs for AADSTS5000820 to identify affected users.
claims.quote: After enforcement is enabled, monitor Microsoft Entra sign-in logs for `AADSTS5000820` errors. Investigate affected users to identify previously undiscovered cross-domain sign-in dependencies or configuration issues.

claims.claim: rootDomains set to none disables cross-domain validation and removes the additional domain-consistency protection.
claims.quote: Disables cross-domain validation. No root-domain matching occurs.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn recommends evaluating compensating controls such as multifactor authentication and Conditional Access when allowing cross-domain sign-in.
claims.quote: Organizations that allow cross-domain sign-in should evaluate compensating controls such as multifactor authentication, Conditional Access, trusted identity-provider governance, privileged access controls, and application-authorization policies.

claims.claim: Learn says to promote a subdomain to a root domain first if a distinct federation configuration is required.
claims.quote: If a distinct federation configuration is required, first [promote the subdomain to a root domain](domains-verify-custom-subdomain#change-subdomain-to-a-root-domain). The policy then validates it independently.

claims.claim: Learn describes sign-in validation, not autonomous actions on accounts.
claims.quote: Searched: "federatedTokenValidationPolicy" "data access" autonomous account actions. Read the feature guide, policy resource and update references; no autonomous account actions are described.

claims.claim: Learn warns that successful testing does not guarantee every tenant sign-in path was exercised.
claims.quote: Successful testing doesn't guarantee that every sign-in path in the tenant has been exercised or that all users are unaffected after enforcement is enabled.
